req.title: Update only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to update a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that a non-author user attempting to POST to /<id>/update must receive HTTP 403. We need: (1) a positive case confirming the author CAN update (2xx), (2) a negative case confirming a non-author gets exactly 403, and (3) a boundary case testing the exact post id boundary (post id=1 exists, post id=0 does not). Additional tests cover the state transition (logged-in non-author vs anonymous) and decision-table combinations to maximise mutation kill rate by asserting exact status codes 403, 200, 302, 404.

tests.name: test_author_can_update_own_post_returns_2xx_or_redirect
preconditions: Database seeded with user id=1 (test/test) and post id=1 authored by user id=1
actions: POST /1/update with title='updated title', body='updated body'
expected: HTTP 302 redirect (successful update redirects to index)
trace: R-FLASKR-019: author is allowed to update — must not receive 403
blog.py update() calls get_post(id, check_author=True); author_id==g.user['id'] so no abort(403)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_author_can_update_own_post_returns_2xx_or_redirect():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'updated title', 'body': 'updated body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 403
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_author_can_update_own_post_returns_2xx_or_redirect()

tests.name: test_non_author_403_and_post_unchanged_in_db
preconditions: Database seeded with post id=1 title='test title' authored by user id=1
actions: POST /1/update with title='evil title', body='evil body'
Query database to confirm post title is still 'test title'
expected: Post title in database remains 'test title' (no mutation occurred)
trace: R-FLASKR-019: 403 must also prevent any data mutation — abort(403) before UPDATE executes
Catches mutations that allow the UPDATE to run despite returning 403
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_non_author_403_and_post_unchanged_in_db():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'other', 'password': 'other'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/update', data={'title': 'evil title', 'body': 'evil body'})
    assert r.status_code == 403
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import get_db
        post = get_db().execute('SELECT title FROM post WHERE id = 1').fetchone()
        assert post['title'] == 'test title'

test_non_author_403_and_post_unchanged_in_db()
